scope: Evidence gate for electrolytic Cu stripping from a dilute liquid Ag-Cu shuttle; not a process validation

claims.claim: For a single homogeneous bath with Cu(I)/Ag(I), an Ag-rich alloy anode satisfying a_Ag(alloy)>a_Cu(alloy), and pure-Cu cathodic deposition required before pure-Ag deposition, the Cu-selective anodic and cathodic R=a_Ag+/a_Cu+ bounds do not overlap, independently of the same-bath standard-potential difference.
assumptions: dimensionless activities in consistent standard states
Cu+ and Ag+ are the operative redox species
cathode compared against pure Cu and pure Ag
limitations: kinetics and overpotential selectivity not bounded
divided-cell or membrane cases are outside the theorem

claims.status: internally computed arithmetic from source-derived/inherited inputs
claims.claim: Using gamma_Cu^infinity(liquid Ag)=3.76 at 1273 K, NIST-JANAF Cu(l)-Cu(s) standard-state correction, and a_Ag approximately 1 gives an anode/cathode R-bound mismatch of about 39.02 at 0.372557 mass% Cu and about 354.5 at 0.040909 mass% Cu.
limitations: a_Ag approximately 1 is a dilute-solvent approximation
gamma_Cu is report-derived, not an electrostripping measurement

claims.claim: No qualifying primary measurement was retrieved for molten Ag-Cu anodic Cu stripping at 1235-1300 K with Cu current efficiency, Ag loss, and electronic conductivity quantified.
limitations: search scope is bounded; absence is not proved

claims.claim: Lu et al. 2024 report 9.1% Cu current efficiency and 0.18 A background current attributed to electronic conduction in spent sulfide electrolysis; Yamaguchi & Ono 2012 report Ag partition to iron/flux in chemical oxidative transfer via Ag; Paeng et al. 2024 report molten-iron oxysulfide Cu reduction from 0.43 wt% to 790 ppmw.
limitations: none is a measured electrostripping test of dilute Ag-Cu at 1235-1300 K
